3.text: are often killed by the Chukchee because they are afraid of anything unusual

4.text: in connection with their herd. Some of the breeders, however, value twins

5.text: highly, asserting that when grown up they will be very swift, and will make

6.text: good racing-reindeer. Therefore when living twins are born into their herd,

7.text: they look for another doe that has just given birth to a dead fawn, and

8.text: carefully wrap one of the living twins into the placenta of the dead fawn to

9.text: make the dam raise it as its own. Of course, this is feasible only in large

10.text: herds, where in calving-time there are daily about twenty or thirty fawns born.

11.text: If a suitable reindeer-dam is wanting, they will sometimes kill some new-born

12.text: fawn and put one of the twins in its place. If they prefer to kill one of the

13.text: twins, they keep a female one, because they believe that it will grow up to

14.text: be a barren doe, fit to use for the harness.¹ Breeding-bucks are best at the

15.text: age of three and four years; later on, their value decreases, although the bulk

16.text: of the body and the dimension of the antlers continue to increase until the

17.text: fifth or sixth year. The doe breeds to the end of her life.²

18.text: The Chukchee herdsmen are careful to select for breeding those does

19.text: that bear the strongest fawns. Those whose fawns have died for several years

20.text: in succession are killed first, when meat is required. The herdsman observes

21.text: the lineage (yɪčhɪˊyɪkwɪn) of his animals through three or four generations in

23.text: Although the Chukchee have a very imperfect system of numerals, and

24.text: never know the exact number of animals in their herd, still they keep a strict

25.text: proportion between its integral parts. Fertile does always form a large majority.

26.text: The largest bucks, aside from those used for breeding, are usually gelded.

27.text: Such geldings and a few barren does are allowed to fatten. The harness-

28.text: reindeer are also geldings, with the exception of a few large barren females

29.text: with large antlers. The majority of the bucks are killed for their skins in

30.text: the first fall of their lives. On an average, there are in a herd, to every

31.text: hundred breeding-does, about a dozen breeding-bucks, from ten to fifteen sledge-

32.text: reindeer, and from sixty to seventy half-grown fawns. In a large herd (Plate

33.text: IV, Fig. 1) there may be to a thousand breeding-does thirty breeding-bucks,

34.text: eighty sledge-reindeer, and from three hundred to four hundred fawns. The

35.text: number of fattened bucks varies from a very few to about as many as there

36.text: are breeding-does. However, large bucks and barren does are highly prized,
